title: Navigation hardening — high-risk on-water reliability fixes
summary: Fix the five high-risk failure modes in the GPS navigation flow that prevent us from assuring real-world trip behavior: (1) timed events stop when the screen sleeps / app is backgrounded, (2) 'notifications' are only TTS+audio with no fallback that reaches a hidden page, (3) GPS permission has no recovery path + the 5s timeout shows a false 'denied' banner + no accuracy filtering, (4) progress uses two inconsistent models (discrete anada / straight-line tornada), (5) arrival + turnaround are order-dependent and the return-safety warning is gated behind reaching the last POI within 50m. Backend (app/server.py) is frozen. Work is split into ordered sessions, each = one agent in one fresh session. The shared file is app/js/screens/navigate.js; each session also owns a distinct NEW module so logic is unit-testable and conflict surface is minimal.

tasks.title: Create nav/trip-progress.js exporting a pure reducer: given {track, activePois, marinaCoords, durationMs, startedAtMs} and a stream of {coords, tMs} fixes, return {phase, activePOIIdx, nextTarget, progressPct, events:[{type,poi?}], returnStartDistM}. No DOM. This becomes the single source of truth navigate.js renders.
tasks.note: Implemented as createTripProgress(cfg) → { update(fix), getSnapshot() }. A factory holding closure state (debounce counters, phase, fired flags) but with NO DOM/globals and NO wall-clock reads (time arrives via each fix's tMs = durationMs - (tMs - startedAtMs)), so it is fully deterministic/unit-testable. Snapshot adds nextTarget, baseDistM, distAlongM, totalAnadaM, returnSafety{remainingMs,etaBackMs,safe} alongside the planned fields. Events: arrival|pass|turnaround|return-unsafe.

tasks.title: Continuous anada progress: project the live position onto the route track (geo helper) and compute progressPct = cumulative distance along track to the projection ÷ total anada distance. Replaces the discrete activePOIIdx/length step model. Tornada stays distance-to-base but measured ALONG the track, not straight-line, so a curving coast reads correctly.
tasks.note: Added geo.js projectOntoTrack(track,coord,cum?) (per-segment equirectangular projection → {distAlongM, crossDistM, segIdx, t, point}) + cumulativeDistancesM(track). Anada progressPct = (distAlong - marinaAlong) / totalAnadaM; totalAnadaM = max(poiAlong) - marinaAlong (max, not list-last, to stay honest if POIs aren't monotonic along the track). Tornada progressPct = 1 - (distAlong - marinaAlong) / (returnStartAlong - marinaAlong) — i.e. remaining track distance to base, not straight-line. Two-period model (owner confirmed 2026-06-24). Unit test 'anada progress is continuous' asserts >5 distinct values (vs 3 the old discrete model could yield).

tasks.title: Tolerant arrival: mark a POI 'reached' when within NAV_ARRIVAL_THRESHOLD_M for ARRIVAL_DEBOUNCE_FIXES consecutive accepted fixes, OR when the paddler is already closer to a later POI / past it along the track by ARRIVAL_SKIP_MARGIN_M (so a skipped or GPS-drifted POI never jams the chain). Announce only genuinely-passed POIs.
tasks.note: Two paths: (1) debounced proximity — N consecutive accepted fixes within NAV_ARRIVAL_THRESHOLD_M → 'arrival' event; (2) a while-loop that advances past any POI whose along-track distance is exceeded by ARRIVAL_SKIP_MARGIN_M → 'pass' event. A single drifted fix can't false-arrive (debounce); a skipped/drifted POI can't jam the chain (margin-skip). navigate.js announces both arrival and pass (both are genuinely-passed) via announceArrival.

tasks.title: Reliable turnaround: flip phase to 'back' on ANY of — last active POI reached, OR furthest-point-along-track passed and now closing toward the marina, OR remaining time low enough that returning is the priority. Decouple the return-safety warning so it can fire even if the last POI was never reached within 50m.
tasks.note: Turnaround flips on ANY of: allPoisDone (idx>=len — includes a margin-skipped last POI), timeCritical (remaining <= etaBack), or closingEarly (got >=50% of the anada AND now closing back by >ARRIVAL_SKIP_MARGIN_M from the furthest point reached). Return-safety is a separate 'return-unsafe' event keyed on remaining < etaBack * RETURN_SAFETY_MARGIN_RATIO while phase==='back' — fires regardless of ever reaching the last POI within 50m. A 'short' turnaround (remaining<etaBack at the flip) pre-sets returnUnsafeFired so the urgent turnaround cue isn't duplicated by return-unsafe.

discoveries: notify() dispatches the SW showNotification off navigator.serviceWorker.ready (a promise) and returns true OPTIMISTICALLY before the notification actually shows; a showNotification rejection falls back to the page Notification constructor inside the .then chain. So the boolean return means 'a channel was attempted', not 'the OS displayed it'. Fine for our use (the foreground channels are the guarantee; notify is best-effort reach), but note it if a future caller wants a hard delivery confirmation.

Permission is requested inside prime(), which runs on BOTH the start tap and every visibilitychange→visible resume. The notifPermissionAsked guard means the resume path never re-prompts; but it also means if the very first prime() (start tap) somehow ran in a context where requestPermission was unavailable, we never retry. Acceptable — start-modal/code-entry are genuine user gestures.

The advisory toast and the overtime banner share the same top anchor (top: max(safe-area+72px, 88px)). They won't realistically collide (the advisory auto-dismisses 9s into the trip; overtime only appears once time runs out), but if a trip's duration were ~0 they could briefly overlap. Cosmetic only.
